answer: Cross-Epoch Kernel Continuity Check. Each identity commits a jade-sealed kernel hash of its decision policy; at epoch boundaries agents must answer held-out challenge probes whose outputs are scored against that prior kernel within a tolerance band. A sable flag marks identities whose cross-epoch drift exceeds the band, and flagged identities face reduced routing weight until re-verified. Sybils pay recurring probe-solvability and drift-accounting costs per identity every epoch, making mass identity upkeep linear and detectable.
